clue.text: See 29
Concentrated Scouse stew follows fine starter for dinner

indicators.note: the stewed piece comes after the letter for fine

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

indicators.note: a stew is a jumbled mixture, so the letters of the word beside it are cooked up anew
the starter of a meal is its first course, so take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A diner fixes their mind on a Liverpool stew after a good first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Scouse is a Liverpool lamb stew, so the surface reads 'Scouse stew' as one dish; in fact 'stew' only signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe attention or force gathered tightly on one point; a synonym pair.

clue.text: Writer of real nonsense

indicators.note: nonsense is jumbled sense, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

explanation.surface: An author of genuine absurdity.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear was famous for nonsense verse, so 'nonsense' does double duty in the surface while only signalling the rearrangement in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear, the Victorian author of limericks and The Owl and the Pussycat, is a writer.

clue.text: Spooner's fair question leads to polite deception

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words found are said with initial sounds exchanged

parts.note: fair hair or skin is light in colour
why is the archetypal question word

explanation.surface: Asking something reasonable leads to a courteous fib.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of LIGHT WHY and you hear the answer phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A small untruth told to spare feelings is exactly a courteous fib, an idiom.

clue.text: Excite Formula One's pure racing

parts.note: Formula One is written F1, with the figure one read as the letter I

indicators.note: racing suggests speeding about wildly, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Grand Prix motor sport in its purest form gets the crowd going.
explanation.walkthrough: F1 becomes FI by reading the numeral as a letter; 'racing' turns PURE into REUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To get someone fired up is to rouse enthusiasm in them, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Coalition party finds Greek character's upset after angry riots

indicators.note: the upturned Greek letter comes after the scrambled riots

parts.note: CON is short for the Conservative Party

indicators.note: angry riots are disordered, so the letters of that word are rearranged
upset in a down clue means knocked over, so the letter's name reads from the bottom up

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A coalition partner discovers a Greek man is upset following violent street riots.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouping of companies or bodies working together is a coalition; near-synonyms.

clue.text: Gangster and murderer reportedly manufacture paraffin

parts.note: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: Cain, in Genesis, killed his brother Abel

explanation.surface: A mobster and a killer, it is said, produce lamp oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufacture' is a link: the pieces make the answer. Paraffin is the British name for kerosene and also for the alkane family of hydrocarbons.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffins are the old chemical name for saturated hydrocarbons, a crossword-friendly synonym.

clue.text: Vocal peak? By 'eck, that's advanced

indicators.note: vocal means spoken out, so the following words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a peak is a height, and 'by 'eck' is a northern English exclamation supplying ECK

explanation.surface: A Yorkshireman marvels at a sophisticated summit, exclaiming 'by 'eck'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By 'eck' is a Yorkshire exclamation of surprise; HEIGHT plus 'ECK, spoken, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Technology that is cutting-edge and sophisticated is described as advanced; a synonym.

clue.text: Economic region's currency traded for no gas

indicators.note: traded for means swapped out in exchange for something else

parts.note: the eurozone is the economic region using the single European currency
the euro is the European currency
no, as in nothing, is shown by O for zero

explanation.surface: In Europe's economic bloc, the currency is swapped for nothing but gas.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap EURO out of EUROZONE for O, leaving O plus ZONE.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of oxygen with three atoms per molecule is a gas, an example of the category.

clue.text: The rabble's hard work turns into double oil spill

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: into means the turned piece goes inside the scrambled letters
an oil spill sends things everywhere, so the letters are scattered
double means take the word twice
turns means the word for work is read backwards

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: The mob's heavy labour turns into cleaning up a twofold oil spill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spill' scrambles the doubled oil, and 'turns' reverses the short word for a musical work before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek phrase for the common people, used in English to mean the masses; a synonym.

clue.text: Saucy maid breaks brute's toe

indicators.note: breaks suggests smashing something apart, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky servant girl damages a bully's toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brute's' keeps its S here: BRUTES TOE gives all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In opera and comedy a soubrette is a pert, flirtatious maidservant role.

clue.text: South American comedy series is a hit

parts.note: M*A*S*H was the long-running American comedy series about an army field hospital

explanation.surface: A Latin American sitcom becomes a big success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one phrase, but South is just S and American attaches to the comedy series.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge commercial success is called a smash; a synonym.

clue.text: Opening numbers: 500,000,000,000?

parts.note: five hundred billion is half a trillion, so take the first half of that word

explanation.surface: A quiz asks for opening figures: five hundred billion?
explanation.walkthrough: Half of TRILLION (eight letters) is TRIL, just as 500,000,000,000 is half a trillion.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the two openings in the nose is a nostril; definition by description.

clue.text: Might they pry or sneak about to gain small exposé, ultimately?

definitions.text: Might they pry or sneak about to gain small exposé, ultimately?

indicators.note: about indicates the letters are moved around

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Busybodies snoop and creep around hoping for a little scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to gain' adds S and the E ending exposé to the scrambled PRY OR SNEAK; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Busybodies who pry into others' affairs are known by this British idiom, so the whole clue describes them.

clue.text: Chief lecturer quaffs gin cocktail with student

indicators.note: to quaff is to drink down, so the lecturer takes the next pieces inside

parts.note: a reader is a senior university lecturer in Britain

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of the spirit are mixed

parts.note: L is for learner, the student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A senior academic downs a gin cocktail with a pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: A Reader is a British academic rank just below professor, so 'lecturer' gives that title.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief instigator of a group, especially of trouble, is its leader; a near-synonym.

clue.text: See 13 down
Female 31's film

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
the answer to 31 is an extraterrestrial, and E.T. is the film about one

explanation.surface: A woman's alien movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like it belongs with 31 (the cinema sense) but is the definition: a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin layer or covering, such as a sheet of ice, is a film; a synonym.

clue.text: Bearing rubbish and litter

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb means to trash, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rubbish collection also takes discarded litter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' is not waste here but the old carried chair; a sedan chair was carried by bearers, so 'Bearing' fits the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter is an enclosed chair carried on poles, which is what a sedan chair is.

clue.text: Say, good clue for O?

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: A setter asks for a good example of a clue for a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the letter O is shaped like the item, so it would make a clue for O.
explanation.definitionFit: The oval shape of a hen's product resembles the letter O, which could stand for it in a clue.

clue.text: Member promoted in Tea Party? It might raise the thickness level

definitions.text: It might raise the thickness level

indicators.note: promoted in a down clue means moved upward, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a leg is a limb, or member

indicators.note: party as a verb means to celebrate wildly, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: An elected member is advanced within the American Tea Party movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tea Party is a US political movement, which makes 'Member promoted' read as politics; 'Party' actually rearranges IN TEA into ATINE.
explanation.definitionFit: This setting agent thickens liquids into jelly, so it raises how thick something is.

clue.text: Silly production of Annie

indicators.note: a production of a show is a staging, so the letters of the name are staged in a new order

explanation.surface: A foolish staging of the musical Annie.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something pointless and foolish; synonyms.

clue.text: Profanities unfold when spoilt son leaves drink

indicators.note: unfold suggests opening out and reshaping, so the long word is rearranged
leaves means the letters of the following word go out of the pool

explanation.surface: Swearing begins when a spoiled boy walks out on his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoilt' is a second scrambling signal for SON; take S, O, N out of PROFANITIES and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A short alcoholic drink taken before a meal to whet the appetite is an aperitif.

clue.text: Orbison returns to cover UK singer, not a US-Swiss singer

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so the backward name surrounds the next piece
returns means the word is read backwards

parts.note: Roy Orbison was the American rock singer

indicators.note: not means the letter after it is removed

parts.note: Adele is the British singer

explanation.surface: Roy Orbison comes back to support a British singer, not an Alpine warbler.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition uses US spelling: one L, as in American English.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who warbles in falsetto in the Swiss Alpine style, spelled the American way.

clue.text: Soap dish upended over top of legs

indicators.note: over here means the reversed dish sits round the next piece
upended in a down clue means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a salad is a dish

indicators.note: top of means the first letter

explanation.surface: A dish is turned upside down over someone's legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upended' turns SALAD into DALAS, which is split by the L from 'top of legs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas was the American television soap opera about the Ewing oil family.

clue.text: Talented man on screen in Surrey village?

definitions.meaning: Tom ... is the title character of the film The Talented Mr ...
A village in Surrey, a county south-west of London

explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Highsmith's charming killer, and also the name of an English village.

clue.text: English composer or hitman?

parts.note: to lam is to hit hard
Bert is a man's name

explanation.surface: Was the English composer actually a contract killer?
explanation.walkthrough: Constant Lambert was an English composer and conductor; the one word 'hitman' splits into its two halves for the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant Lambert, the twentieth-century English composer of The Rio Grande, bears this surname.

clue.text: Loveless tabloid hack dismisses boss's head girl

indicators.note: hack means to chop about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: love means zero in tennis, O, and less means it goes

indicators.note: head means the first letter, and dismisses says it leaves

explanation.surface: A heartless tabloid journalist sacks the boss's head girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismisses' joins 'Loveless' in removing letters: take O and B from TABLOID and rearrange TALID.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilda is a girl's name, as in the actress Tilda Swinton.

clue.text: See 8
Strong man possesses single talent

indicators.note: possesses means holds within, so the single letter goes inside

parts.note: potent means strong
Al is a man's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A powerful man has a singular gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Latent ability not yet developed is called potential, a near-synonym for talent.

clue.text: Prophet discarding most of the bread

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: Nathan was the Old Testament prophet who rebuked King David

indicators.note: discarding means letters are dropped from the prophet's name

explanation.surface: A prophet throws away most of his loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Most of THE is TH; NATHAN without TH leaves NAAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan is a leavened South Asian flatbread, an example of the category.

clue.text: Pine shop condemned for bad deliveries

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it

indicators.note: condemned property is ruined, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: A pine furniture shop is shut down over poor deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a long hop is a short-pitched, easily hit ball, a poor delivery by the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: These short-pitched balls in cricket are easy to hit, so they count as poor bowling.

clue.text: Cameron (he vacillates) changing sides like this one?

definitions.text: Cameron (he vacillates) changing sides like this one?

indicators.note: vacillates means wavers back and forth, so the letters move about
changing sides swaps right for left, R becoming L

explanation.surface: David Cameron, wavering, switches allegiance like a famously changeable lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L are right and left; swap them in CAMERON and rearrange CAMELON with HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lizard that changes colour to suit its surroundings stands for a person who switches positions.

clue.text: Foreign film

definitions.meaning: the 1979 Ridley Scott science-fiction horror film

explanation.definitionFit: The word means foreign, and is also the title of the Ridley Scott film with Sigourney Weaver.
